summary: Fetch integer, binary32 and full-group barrier instructions for cooperating threads with separate global and shared storage and checked access bounds; compose instruction segments only after matching their actual program positions.
Derive repeated-barrier ordering and complete memory labels from actual executions; force single-writer publication through the existing memory constraints.
Construct a completed two-thread, two-round computed-publication witness with checked read sources and no circular dependencies; concrete layer ownership, timing and execution proofs remain separate.

Derive initial or last-store read origins from concrete executions, construct chronological graph certificates, and prove admission under the existing restricted memory constraints with actual barrier order.

For programs without jumps or scalar exits, derive strict per-thread instruction order and timing around actual barrier completions for arbitrary candidate runs; visibility still requires a proved unique writer for each location.
Prove agreement with a data-independent address calculation after checking every instruction, then recover actual emitted load/store addresses and retained predicate truth under arbitrary scheduling.

Recover the actual exit of a halted lane and the execution step at every earlier crossed site; passing a synchronization site requires an emitted collective completion, while an enabled memory store still needs its guard proved.
Derive final memory contents from the actual stores independently of proposed load values; this does not impose chronological read semantics.
Extend the instruction machine to independent groups with private scratch and barriers; the child contract records the separate state of combined correctness, execution existence and composition.
remaining: Straight-line candidate traces now have strict per-thread instruction order, unique execution of each thread/site pair and strict ordering of completed barrier sites. Actual completion splits derive producer/consumer timing from instruction sites, and the visibility rule uses those derived facts. The address-control projection retains the dense kernel's chosen integer registers, all address registers and predicate zero; instruction compatibility is proved before use. Other register layouts require another compatibility check or generalization. Site-crossing and halt-origin rules recover actual memory evaluations and barrier completions. Kernel proofs must still discharge guard conditions and connect consumer addresses and allowed values to their producers. Launch validation and general barrier forms remain unimplemented. Concrete-read admission is a sufficient witness construction, not a characterization of all PTX executions.

from.quote:
A selected software runner reads the current arrays and chooses the checked
binary32 reference result. Its steps are proved to be candidate-machine steps;
this alone does not make the resulting memory graph admissible. A concrete-read
execution additionally retains that each load used the current array rather than
a freely proposed word. This restriction applies only to an existence witness;
the general candidate relation and permitted floating-point results stay unchanged.
Replaying the recorded loads and stores must reproduce the arrays, including
the value observed by each load. This supplies evidence for constructing read
sources: every load must use the initial word when there is no preceding store,
or the value of the last preceding store to that location in the trace. Global
and shared locations are tracked separately. This does not itself discharge the
memory constraints. A selected concrete-read trace can supply a chronological
certificate: initial writes precede program events, each load uses its last
preceding write, and writes to the same location follow their trace order.
The certificate must also respect the ordering derived from actual barrier
arrivals and completions. Graph entries are grouped by thread, so their list
indices are not a global chronology. Each program event instead keeps its
position in the full instruction trace, including non-memory events; initial
writes occupy a separate earlier range. A proved source function selects a
compatible initial or last program write for every read. This is a mathematical
existence construction, not an executable graph-extraction tool. Its proof
establishes the existing restricted memory constraints and excludes circular
chains through order and read-source edges. It does not impose this selected
chronology on all permitted executions or establish general PTX semantics.

A two-thread witness supplies that additional proof: threads publish inputs, synchronize,
compute sums, publish to fresh locations, synchronize again and store the peer's
result to separate outputs. It works for arbitrary input words, reaches exit in
both threads, and satisfies the original memory constraints. A chronological
certificate also excludes circular dependence through read sources. This is an
existence example, not a restriction on all candidate executions or a full layer
implementation.

The final contents of a memory word follow the actual stores: the last store
to that word supplies its final value, and a word with no store keeps its initial
contents. This fact holds even when load values are freely proposed. It does not
